#+TITLE: Differentiable Polish — gradient-based local refinement after DIRECT, the z-signal, and what is actually transferable to a hand-written CUDA stack
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: differentiable-polish

* Summary

A gradient-polish stage after DIRECT is feasible in this stack, but only if it optimizes a *smooth surrogate* — the production DIRECT_DILATION cost is a piecewise-constant function of pose (binary silhouette + int-atomic reductions), so its gradient is zero almost everywhere and undefined at pixel flips. The surrogate already exists in the codebase: the chamfer distance-map term (DistanceMapMetric), whose gradient is the standard analytic-silhouette-gradient: Σ over rendered edge pixels of ∇D(p)·(projection Jacobian). That Jacobian needs only the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics that FillTriangleKernel already computes and throws away. The depth channel is the angle's main myth to puncture: a front-surface z/w buffer is 80% machinery-present (the DRR fill already interpolates perspective-correct z), but a depth channel does *not* make z observable in single-plane fluoro — the 6.31 mm z gap is the magnification limit, and the only real z-fixes are biplane (already supported) or a known-geometry prior. Verdict: GO for a budget-accounted polish stage (chamfer surrogate, analytic Jacobian, ~2-3 weeks) scored by angle 03's harness as a DIRECT-only vs DIRECT+polish ablation arm; NO-GO for the photometric DRR-gradient and torch-bridge routes.

* Key Findings

** The production cost is piecewise-constant in pose — the gradient of the existing cost is not a usable signal, and this is the load-bearing constraint on everything else
- FastImplantDilationMetric reduces with int atomicAdd over binary comparisons (DILATED_PIXEL/EDGE_PIXEL vs WHITE in the dilated comparison) and DistanceMapMetric sums int distance values over a *discrete* edge-pixel set; both change only when a rendered pixel flips 0↔255 as vertices cross pixel centers. The render itself (RenderEngine::Render) writes a binary silhouette. [Source: repo — src/compute/fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu, src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu, src/compute/DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:58-92]
- Consequence: finite-difference on the production cost gives zero or garbage Jacobians for any step not straddling a flip boundary; there is no gradient to "polish" through the production metric. Any polish stage must (a) optimize a smooth surrogate, and (b) verify the result with the production cost — the surrogate is a *search* objective, the production cost stays the *arbiter* (same relationship as angle 03's appearance gate vs cost math).
- Also note the existing metric's int reduction truncates (double→int atomicAdd truncation is already listed as bug 6 in the local recon) — a polish surrogate must use float accumulation.
- Confidence: high (source-verified)
- Relevance to this project: kills option (b) of accountable question 1 (finite-difference on the existing cost) before it starts; forces the surrogate architecture that the harness can actually measure.

** The smooth surrogate already exists: DistanceMapMetric is a chamfer loss, and its gradient is the standard analytic silhouette gradient
- DistanceMapMetric = Σ_{rendered edge pixels} distance_map[p] / (count+0.1) — a mean-chamfer of the rendered silhouette edge to the target (fluoro) edge; the distance transform makes it Lipschitz with an image-space gradient ∇D computable numerically from the distance map itself. [Source: repo — src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu; include/compute/frame.h (SetDistanceMap)]
- The standard differentiable-registration gradient is dL/dθ = Σ_{p ∈ E(θ)} ∇D(p)·(dp/dθ) + a boundary term from pixels crossing the edge set; the boundary term is what analytic AA (Modular Primitives) or soft coverage (SoftRas/DIB-R) smooths, and it is small relative to the ∇D term inside the DIRECT basin (few flips per step at convergence). Published relatives of exactly this gradient: "Analytical Derivatives for Differentiable Renderer: 3D Pose Estimation" (arXiv:1906.07870) and "3D/2D Registration of Angiograms using Silhouette-based Differentiable Rendering" (arXiv:2501.14918). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.07870; https://arxiv.org/html/2501.14918]
- dp/dθ is analytic for a rigid body: projected p = (fx·X/Z + cx, fy·Y/Z + cy) with (X,Y,Z) affine in the pose θ (R·v + t), so the 2×6 projection Jacobian is a ~50-line kernel. This is the "Modular-Primitives-style analytic silhouette gradient" in its minimal form — no soft rasterizer, no AA pass required for the MVP.
- Confidence: high (the math is standard; the codebase already contains both ingredients)
- Relevance: this is the minimal viable gradient signal (accountable question 1): analytic projection Jacobian + numerical ∇D from the existing distance map, at 1 render per step. The honest baseline to implement *first* (measurement-first) is forward/central differences on this same surrogate (6-12 renders/step, zero new rasterizer code) — it establishes whether gradient polish wins at all before the analytic investment.

** FillTriangleKernel already computes the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics that the gradient needs — and discards them
- FillTriangleKernel computes the unnormalized barycentrics (a, b, c, denominator) for the inside test and only writes 255 to the image. Writing (triangleIndex, a, b, c) out for filled pixels is the Modular-Primitives per-pixel output minus the NDC z: exactly the (ID, u, v) tuple the backward pass consumes. The renderer also knows the projected positions and (in the DRR twin) per-vertex camera z, so the un-projected 3D source point of each edge pixel is recoverable. [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu FillTriangleKernel; Modular Primitives rasterizer outputs (ID, u, v, zc/wc) + 2×2 barycentric Jacobian per https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2011.03277]
- Cost: one extra device buffer (float4 per filled pixel) + ~10 lines in the fill kernel. The stride/prefix/bounding-box launch scheme is untouched.
- Confidence: high (source-verified)
- Relevance: this is what makes the analytic route cheap — the rasterizer is already 80% of a differentiable rasterizer; only the output staging and the backward scatter-add are missing.

** The depth channel: machinery is 80% present, but a depth channel does NOT fix the z-weak axis in single-plane fluoro — the honest finding this angle exists to deliver
- Where z comes from today: the silhouette path (Render) computes per-vertex camera z (tZ) in WorldToPixelKernel and *discards it*; the DRR path stores it (dev_transf_vertex_zs_) and DRR_FillTriangleKernel interpolates per-pixel perspective-correct z via the rational formula (tvz1·tvz2·tvz3·denominator)/(a·tvz2·tvz3 + b·tvz1·tvz3 + c·tvz1·tvz2) — which is exactly 1/(λ1/z1 + λ2/z2 + λ3/z3), i.e. the perspective-correct interpolated camera z at the pixel. There is no z-testing anywhere (all triangles draw; backfaces are sign-flipped in the DRR accumulation). A front-surface NDC-style depth buffer (this stack's "z/w" ≡ −tZ_cam, positive toward the detector) needs only a min-z test in the fill + a float buffer — and dev_z_line_values_ (width×height float) is already allocated and reusable. [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu:430-520, src/compute/render_drr_engine.cu DRR_WorldToPixelKernel + DRR_FillTriangleKernel, include/compute/render_engine.cuh dev_z_line_values_/dev_transf_vertex_zs_]
- Why it does not fix z: (a) there is *no target depth* in a single-plane fluoro to compare a rendered depth against — a depth-difference term only exists in synthetic self-supervised ablations (render at known pose → optimize), against a registered bone model / known-geometry prior, or in biplane; (b) the observed z gap is the magnification limit — z-translation is only observable through scale (6.31 mm z gap vs 0.16/0.08 in-plane in baseline.json; angle 03's probe arithmetic: <1% scale change over ±15 mm at ~1.1 m), and no gradient changes what is observable; (c) NVDiffrast — the reference implementation of Modular Primitives — intentionally does *not* backprop through the z/w channel (issue #70: the z/w output's gradients are not propagated; the meaningful gradients are the vertex-position ones). [Source: repo — test/golden/baseline.json tolerances.observed_max_gap_vs_golden; https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast/issues/70 (search-verified content, page fetch failed); https://nvlabs.github.io/nvdiffrast/]

#+TITLE: Differentiable Polish — gradient-based local refinement after DIRECT, the z-signal, and what is actually transferable to a hand-written CUDA stack
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: differentiable-polish

* Summary

A gradient-polish stage after DIRECT is feasible in this stack, but only if it optimizes a *smooth surrogate* — the production DIRECT_DILATION cost is a piecewise-constant function of pose (binary silhouette + int-atomic reductions), so its gradient is zero almost everywhere and undefined at pixel flips. The surrogate already exists in the codebase: the chamfer distance-map term (DistanceMapMetric), whose gradient is the standard analytic-silhouette-gradient: Σ over rendered edge pixels of ∇D(p)·(projection Jacobian). That Jacobian needs only the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics that FillTriangleKernel already computes and throws away. The depth channel is the angle's main myth to puncture: a front-surface z/w buffer is 80% machinery-present (the DRR fill already interpolates perspective-correct z), but a depth channel does *not* make z observable in single-plane fluoro — the 6.31 mm z gap is the magnification limit, and the only real z-fixes are biplane (already supported) or a known-geometry prior. Verdict: GO for a budget-accounted polish stage (chamfer surrogate, analytic Jacobian, ~2-3 weeks) scored by angle 03's harness as a DIRECT-only vs DIRECT+polish ablation arm; NO-GO for the photometric DRR-gradient and torch-bridge routes.

* Key Findings

** The production cost is piecewise-constant in pose — the gradient of the existing cost is not a usable signal, and this is the load-bearing constraint on everything else
- FastImplantDilationMetric reduces with int atomicAdd over binary comparisons (DILATED_PIXEL/EDGE_PIXEL vs WHITE in the dilated comparison) and DistanceMapMetric sums int distance values over a *discrete* edge-pixel set; both change only when a rendered pixel flips 0↔255 as vertices cross pixel centers. The render itself (RenderEngine::Render) writes a binary silhouette. [Source: repo — src/compute/fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu, src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu, src/compute/DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:58-92]
- Consequence: finite-difference on the production cost gives zero or garbage Jacobians for any step not straddling a flip boundary; there is no gradient to "polish" through the production metric. Any polish stage must (a) optimize a smooth surrogate, and (b) verify the result with the production cost — the surrogate is a *search* objective, the production cost stays the *arbiter* (same relationship as angle 03's appearance gate vs cost math).
- Also note the existing metric's int reduction truncates (double→int atomicAdd truncation is already listed as bug 6 in the local recon) — a polish surrogate must use float accumulation.
- Confidence: high (source-verified)
- Relevance to this project: kills option (b) of accountable question 1 (finite-difference on the existing cost) before it starts; forces the surrogate architecture that the harness can actually measure.

** The smooth surrogate already exists: DistanceMapMetric is a chamfer loss, and its gradient is the standard analytic silhouette gradient
- DistanceMapMetric = Σ_{rendered edge pixels} distance_map[p] / (count+0.1) — a mean-chamfer of the rendered silhouette edge to the target (fluoro) edge; the distance transform makes it Lipschitz with an image-space gradient ∇D computable numerically from the distance map itself. [Source: repo — src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu; include/compute/frame.h (SetDistanceMap)]
- The standard differentiable-registration gradient is dL/dθ = Σ_{p ∈ E(θ)} ∇D(p)·(dp/dθ) + a boundary term from pixels crossing the edge set; the boundary term is what analytic AA (Modular Primitives) or soft coverage (SoftRas/DIB-R) smooths, and it is small relative to the ∇D term inside the DIRECT basin (few flips per step at convergence). Published relatives of exactly this gradient: "Analytical Derivatives for Differentiable Renderer: 3D Pose Estimation" (arXiv:1906.07870) and "3D/2D Registration of Angiograms using Silhouette-based Differentiable Rendering" (arXiv:2501.14918). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.07870; https://arxiv.org/html/2501.14918]
- dp/dθ is analytic for a rigid body: projected p = (fx·X/Z + cx, fy·Y/Z + cy) with (X,Y,Z) affine in the pose θ (R·v + t), so the 2×6 projection Jacobian is a ~50-line kernel. This is the "Modular-Primitives-style analytic silhouette gradient" in its minimal form — no soft rasterizer, no AA pass required for the MVP.
- Confidence: high (the math is standard; the codebase already contains both ingredients)
- Relevance: this is the minimal viable gradient signal (accountable question 1): analytic projection Jacobian + numerical ∇D from the existing distance map, at 1 render per step. The honest baseline to implement *first* (measurement-first) is forward/central differences on this same surrogate (6-12 renders/step, zero new rasterizer code) — it establishes whether gradient polish wins at all before the analytic investment.

** FillTriangleKernel already computes the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics that the gradient needs — and discards them
- FillTriangleKernel computes the unnormalized barycentrics (a, b, c, denominator) for the inside test and only writes 255 to the image. Writing (triangleIndex, a, b, c) out for filled pixels is the Modular-Primitives per-pixel output minus the NDC z: exactly the (ID, u, v) tuple the backward pass consumes. The renderer also knows the projected positions and (in the DRR twin) per-vertex camera z, so the un-projected 3D source point of each edge pixel is recoverable. [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu FillTriangleKernel; Modular Primitives rasterizer outputs (ID, u, v, zc/wc) + 2×2 barycentric Jacobian per https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2011.03277]
- Cost: one extra device buffer (float4 per filled pixel) + ~10 lines in the fill kernel. The stride/prefix/bounding-box launch scheme is untouched.
- Confidence: high (source-verified)
- Relevance: this is what makes the analytic route cheap — the rasterizer is already 80% of a differentiable rasterizer; only the output staging and the backward scatter-add are missing.

** The depth channel: machinery is 80% present, but a depth channel does NOT fix the z-weak axis in single-plane fluoro — the honest finding this angle exists to deliver
- Where z comes from today: the silhouette path (Render) computes per-vertex camera z (tZ) in WorldToPixelKernel and *discards it*; the DRR path stores it (dev_transf_vertex_zs_) and DRR_FillTriangleKernel interpolates per-pixel perspective-correct z via the rational formula (tvz1·tvz2·tvz3·denominator)/(a·tvz2·tvz3 + b·tvz1·tvz3 + c·tvz1·tvz2) — which is exactly 1/(λ1/z1 + λ2/z2 + λ3/z3), i.e. the perspective-correct interpolated camera z at the pixel. There is no z-testing anywhere (all triangles draw; backfaces are sign-flipped in the DRR accumulation). A front-surface NDC-style depth buffer (this stack's "z/w" ≡ −tZ_cam, positive toward the detector) needs only a min-z test in the fill + a float buffer — and dev_z_line_values_ (width×height float) is already allocated and reusable. [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu:430-520, src/compute/render_drr_engine.cu DRR_WorldToPixelKernel + DRR_FillTriangleKernel, include/compute/render_engine.cuh dev_z_line_values_/dev_transf_vertex_zs_]
- Why it does not fix z: (a) there is *no target depth* in a single-plane fluoro to compare a rendered depth against — a depth-difference term only exists in synthetic self-supervised ablations (render at known pose → optimize), against a registered bone model / known-geometry prior, or in biplane; (b) the observed z gap is the magnification limit — z-translation is only observable through scale (6.31 mm z gap vs 0.16/0.08 in-plane in baseline.json; angle 03's probe arithmetic: <1% scale change over ±15 mm at ~1.1 m), and no gradient changes what is observable; (c) NVDiffrast — the reference implementation of Modular Primitives — intentionally does *not* backprop through the z/w channel (issue #70: the z/w output's gradients are not propagated; the meaningful gradients are the vertex-position ones). [Source: repo — test/golden/baseline.json tolerances.observed_max_gap_vs_golden; https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast/issues/70 (search-verified content, page fetch failed); https://nvlabs.github.io/nvdiffrast/]
- What the depth machinery IS worth: (i) occlusion-aware visibility gradients — Modular Primitives' premise "a 3D primitive with no effect on the image receives zero gradient" requires knowing which triangle owns each pixel (z-test), which the renderer lacks today; (ii) a synthetic-depth loss in the harness's self-supervised arm (a genuine z test *when a target depth exists*); (iii) the z-line-integral (dev_z_line_values_) is a stronger quantitative z signal than front-depth (it shifts by ≈Δz·path-length under z-translation) but is an X-ray-attenuation proxy — unobservable for a saturated metal implant and only useful in the ML/DRR pathway (DiffDRR-style).
- The real z-fixes: biplane (the codebase already has it — calibration_.convert_Pose_A_to_Pose_B and a biplane branch in DIRECT_DILATION) and the known-geometry prior (implant constrained to a registered bone). This matches the prior-run ML angle's finding 8 ("if the ML pathway is to beat the monoplane z gap, biplane is the evidence-backed direction").
- Confidence: high on the machinery facts (source-verified + NVDiffrast issue); high on the observability argument (analytic); medium on the exact clinical z-benefit of biplane/prior until measured
- Relevance: answer to accountable question 2 — the depth channel is a *gradient-quality and ablation-signal* feature, not a z fix; the harness should test it as such (self-supervised depth arm), and the z-profile probe (angle 03) should first confirm the chamfer surrogate's valley is deeper than the dilated-overlap valley — that is the precondition for any polish z-win.

- Kernel structure (concrete): ChamferGradientKernel — grid over the chamfer CROP (the exact diff_kernel bounds DistanceMapMetric computes from the render's bounding box ± dilation: max(bbox[0]−d, d), min(bbox[2]+d, width−d−1), etc. — host-computed after Render()'s D2H bbox sync, so the gradient's pixel set equals the value's pixel set BY CONSTRUCTION); one thread per crop pixel; skip unless dev_image[p] == EDGE_PIXEL; read dev_fill_attrib_[p] → (triangleIndex, u, v); read the triangle's 3 model-space vertices from dev_triangles_ (9 floats, static); X = R·(u·V1 + v·V2 + (1−u−v)·V3) + t; build the 2×6 Jacobian; g_j += ∇D(p)·∂p/∂θ_j. This is a pixel-grid kernel (not the fragment stream) deliberately: it processes each pixel once, which dedupes the overlapping-triangle case that a fragment-stream iteration would double-count (R2-3's last-writer attribute resolves ownership). [Source: repo — src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu (crop formula), src/compute/render_engine.cu (fragment stream semantics)]
- Float accumulation + the determinism rule (the part that is easy to get wrong): the gradient MUST accumulate in float (never the production path's int truncation — the distance-map index bug and the int-atomic truncation are explicitly NOT to be copied), AND the accumulation must be bit-deterministic, because the ablation runner's rerun_identical determinism twin (ablation.json determinism block) would trip on a float-atomic gradient — Contradiction 3's int-determinism doctrine extends to the polish by construction. Design: per-block shared-memory reduction to 6 floats → dev_chamfer_gradient_partials_[6·nBlocks] (≈24 KB at nBlocks ≈ 1000) → a second 1-block kernel reduces the partials in fixed block order → the 6-float gradient. Two kernels, ~30 lines; float atomicAdd into the partial array is acceptable ONLY if the run records the gradient hash as informational — spec the ordered reduction as the default. Reset via cudaMemset before each call (6·(1+nBlocks)·4 B ≈ 24 KB — cheap, and the eval path's no-cudaMalloc rule is preserved: the partial array is allocated once in the polish stage's initialization). [Source: repo — test/golden/ablation.json schema (angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org R2-4 determinism block); synthesis Contradiction 3]
- Production-parity matching rules (verified semantics): (a) the polish RenderEngine is constructed with use_backface_culling = TRUE (production parity; the round-2 backface finding: ON paints 1-px speckle per backface triangle while the image bbox is ON/OFF-identical, so the surrogate/gradient pixel sets differ from the oracle's OFF render only in bounded speckle — and the FINAL pose is still scored by the oracle's OFF renderer for the gate, so the two conventions never mix inside one number); (b) leaf dilation = 1 for every surrogate, gradient, and verification call; (c) the distance map is the frame's existing GPUFrame (never recomputed); (d) the gradient crop = the value's crop (above). [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu (backface semantics, BoundingBoxSizesKernel size-1 comment), angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org Round 2 (backface speckle correction), test/golden/baseline.json (dilation_px leaf 1)]
- The gradient-twin gate between the FD MVP and the analytic kernel: at 3-5 poses per run (the start, the leaf optimum, and 2-3 intermediate accepted poses), compare g_analytic vs central-difference g_fd (12 renders per check). PASS = per-axis |g_a − g_fd| ≤ 0.5·|g_fd| + floor with matching signs; FAIL = record, fall back to FD for the rest of the run, and file the analytic-kernel bug (candidate causes, in order: last-writer attribute mismatch in overlap regions; the omitted boundary term — pixels entering/leaving the EDGE set; ∇D convention at the crop border). This is the empirical gate that decides whether the boundary term (the one approximate piece of the math) is negligible in THIS geometry — it is verified, not assumed, and it is exactly what arXiv:1906.07870's treatment would formalize if it is not (R2-6). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.07870; angle 06 Round 1 "smooth surrogate" (boundary-term discussion)]
- Cost per step (analytic arm): 1 render/step — the acceptance verification render at θ_k is the base for the gradient kernel (FastImplantDilationMetric edge-marks it, the chamfer value call reads it, the gradient kernel reads it after — all on the same image state; EDGE pixels survive the dilation pass, R2-1); then θ_{k+1} = clamp(θ_k − α·h·sign(g), leaf_box) with the same α-halving acceptance rule. At B_p = 1000: ~800 accepted steps, capped by polish_max_steps = 500 (default) → the analytic arm usually stops on the cap or the α-exhaustion stall, whichever first; the evals actually used are recorded. [Source: angle 06 Round 1 "hybrid loop" + "feasibility verdicts" (1 render/step, +1 week)]
- Confidence: high on the math and kernel structure (every formula traces to verified code); medium on the boundary-term magnitude and the overlap-fraction error until the twin check runs (they are measurements by design).
- Relevance to this project: this is the +1-week analytic increment over the FD MVP, with its own falsifiable gate (the twin check) and its own determinism requirement (the ordered reduction — a requirement that only becomes visible when you trace the polish through the ablation runner's rerun_identical assertion).

#### R2-5 — The ablation arm that arbitrates contradiction 6: THREE arms at equal cumulative budget, the B-arm budget-gift control, the IoU gate, per-axis gaps, and the sample size that makes it conclusive
- The round-1 two-arm design had a confound this round's redesign removes: DIRECT-only@B vs DIRECT@(B−B_p)+polish@B_p cannot separate "polish added quality" from "the 1000 evals were spent better by polish than DIRECT would have spent them" — the budget gift itself is the alternative explanation. The pre-registered design is therefore three arms, all from the same start seed, all on the same frame:
  - **A: DIRECT-only@35k** (production shape 20/25/30/35k) — the reference.
  - **B: DIRECT-only@34k** (leaf 5000→4000; cumulative 20/25/30/34k) — the budget-gift control: it is what DIRECT does with the budget BEFORE the polish gets it.
  - **C: DIRECT@34k + polish@B_p = 1000** (DIRECT as in B, then RunPolishStage at the leaf optimum; polish evals push the counter to 35k).
  C wins only if C beats B (polish used its 1000 evals better than DIRECT would have — the marginal-value test) AND C ≥ A (no net loss at equal total budget — the equal-budget test). If C > B but C < A, polish added nothing net: the 1000 evals were better spent by DIRECT. This is the honest arbitrage of the "12x" thesis: at FIXED total budget the thesis reduces to a final-quality comparison; the "fewer evals" reading only materializes when the DIRECT budget itself shrinks (the ML-initializer pathway), which the arm records but does not claim. [Source: angle 06 Round 1 "12x thesis"; synthesis Contradiction 6; repo — test/golden/baseline.json budget_per_stage]
- Budget bookkeeping (round-1 rule, made exact): every polish surrogate eval AND every trial verification increments cost_function_calls_, so C's counter lands on 20/25/30/34k during DIRECT and 35k after polish; the stage-bookkeeping gate (angle 03: costCalls() on the cumulative caps) applies to A/B/C identically. Surrogate evals are counted at parity with production evals — conservative FOR polish (a surrogate eval is cheaper: ~5 launches + 2 syncs vs ~15 launches + 5 syncs), so a win under parity accounting is a win a fortiori; a time-based variant is a recorded follow-up, not an MVP claim. [Source: angle 06 Round 1 "budget semantics"; angles/05-compute-perf.org sync inventory]
- Gates and recordings (per unit, per arm): the IoU ≥ 0.85 appearance gate on the ORACLE renderer (backface OFF — the same comparator as DIRECT-only's final measurement, so the two arms are never compared through different conventions; baseline.json silhouette_iou_threshold 0.85); per-px L1 banded-record; per-axis pose gaps vs fem.jts (pose_gap_vs_golden_mm_deg — the schema field angle 03 already defines); z-gap banded-informational; final production cost; evals-to-gate via a data profile (IoU sampled at 1k-eval checkpoints — 35 extra renders per run, trivial; C's verification evals give a dense profile for the final 1000). ablation.json gains a polish block: {arm, surrogate: "DistanceMapMetric", gradient: "forward-difference|analytic", steps, evals_used, final_production_cost, h: [6], alpha_halvings, per_axis_gap_mm_deg, iou, z_gap_mm, precondition: {g1..g4: bool}, determinism: {run_hash, rerun_identical}} and the z_profiles records gain a term field {term: "full|chamfer|dilated"}. [Source: angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org R2-2 + R2-4 (schema); repo — test/golden/baseline.json tolerances]
- Sample size and what is conclusive (honest power math): the sampling unit is (frame × start seed) — DIRECT is deterministic per seed (RNG-free bookkeeping), and the polish is deterministic given the ordered-reduction gradient (R2-4), so the per-unit variance is entirely across units, and the design is paired (A/B/C from the same seed). For a paired one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank, α = 0.05, power 0.8: detecting a 1σ improvement needs N ≈ 12 pairs; detecting 0.5σ needs N ≈ 34. The in-repo pool is Kneel_1's 3 frames (baseline.json expected_pose_per_frame × 3) — so the pre-registered unit construction is 3 frames × 4 start seeds = 12 units (seeds: truth + one in-plane x, one in-plane y, one z perturbation chosen from the perturbation suite's Δ set, e.g. ±2 mm / +5 mm z — pre-registered in the manifest), which is **conclusive at 1σ effects and honestly underpowered below that** (the arm reports the achieved power; a 0.5σ outcome is recorded as "inconclusive", not as a null). σ is estimated from the per-axis gap distribution across the 12 DIRECT-only units after the first nightly run. Subject0 (example_studies/Subject0, Cam1/Cam2 biplane with STLs) is a future frame pool only — different fixtures/calibration, out of scope for the MVP arm. Cost: 12 units × 3 arms × ~15 min (35k shape at the verified 20-60 evals/s) ≈ 9 h on the 3090 → the full matrix is nightly; CI runs 1 frame × 3 arms on the Moré & Wild reduced shape. [Source: repo — test/golden/baseline.json (3 frames, budget), example_studies/{Kneel_1,Subject0}; angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org R2-1 (perturbation Δ set) + R2-4 (ci/nightly split)]
- The landing rule (round-1, made operational): polish ships behind enable_polish_/polish_budget_/polish_max_steps only when, over the 12-unit matrix: (a) the IoU ≥ 0.85 gate passes on every unit in every arm; (b) C beats B on median final production cost AND median in-plane gap (paired test at the pre-registered effect size); (c) C ≥ A on the same (no net loss at equal budget); (d) no per-axis gap regression beyond the minimal-detectable-regression table (the perturbation suite's deliverable — a regression the gate can see is a fail by definition); (e) the precondition gate (R2-1) recorded, and any z-gap claim is made only if G1-G4 held. The "12x fewer evals" figure is recorded as a target, not a justification, and is structurally capped at the leaf-phase win (round-1 analysis stands). [Source: angle 06 Round 1 "Recommended go/no-go"; synthesis Contradiction 6]
- Confidence: high on the mechanics (seams, schema, budget shape all source-verified; the B-arm confound is a design argument); medium on the effect-size pre-registration (σ is unmeasured until the first nightly run — reported, not assumed).
- Relevance to this project: this is the instrument that closes the run's only explicitly low-confidence claim (Contradiction 6) with a design that cannot mistake a budget gift for a polish win — and it plugs into angle 03's runner with a schema extension, not new infrastructure.

#### R2-6 — Zotero pull list with per-paper expected value: what each paper changes about the MVP or the NO-GO list
1. **NVDiffrast** (nvlabs/nvdiffrast, https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast) — expected value: (a) the reference CUDA backward kernel shapes — their rasterize_bwd is a scatter-add over triangle IDs, the exact accumulation pattern the MVP's gradient kernel uses, confirming the design before it is written; (b) the attribute-gradient chain incl. the 2×2 barycentric Jacobian (Eq. 2 in Modular Primitives) — which the MVP does NOT need for a rigid body (R2-3), so the paper's highest value here is the *negative*: it shows exactly what the MVP saves; (c) the analytic post-process AA implementation = the concrete spec for the boundary-term correction IF the FD-twin check shows the term is non-negligible; (d) the z/w no-gradient policy (issue #70, search-verified round 1) — reconfirms NDC-depth stays off the polish path. Changes to the MVP: none required; upgrades the fallback list with a copyable AA spec. [Source: https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast, https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast/issues/70, https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2011.03277]
2. **"Analytical Derivatives for Differentiable Renderer: 3D Pose Estimation"** (arXiv:1906.07870, https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.07870) — expected value: (a) the boundary-term derivation (pixels entering/leaving the rendered region under pose perturbation) — the ONE piece of the MVP math that is approximate, and the paper is the closest published treatment of exactly this discrete-sampling derivative; (b) their 6-DoF pose-estimation protocol from silhouette gradients — a ready-made validation recipe the FD-twin check borrows; (c) their edge-pixel-only summation (same as the MVP's EDGE-set sum). Changes: decides whether the analytic kernel needs a ~20-line boundary-term addition; if yes, supplies the exact term. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.07870]
3. **Gablonsky's thesis + "A Locally-Biased form of the DIRECT Algorithm"** (https://repository.lib.ncsu.edu/items/37f7120b-c41e-4267-83d7-5cea4e770b4d; DOI 10.1023/A:1017930332101) — expected value: (a) the DIRECT+local-search hybrid's termination theory — the polish's STOP rule (production-cost stall over N steps + α-exhaustion) gets a literature-anchored justification; (b) the locally-biased DIRECT algorithm itself — the DIRECT-side upgrade that makes the hybrid self-consistent IF the arm wins (bias selection toward the current optimum; related to but distinct from angle 01's -gb refinement); (c) their test methodology — a battery protocol angle 01's analytic battery can reuse for the polish surrogate. Changes: the STOP/re-seed loop design; nothing to the kernels. [Source: https://repository.lib.ncsu.edu/items/37f7120b-c41e-4267-83d7-5cea4e770b4d; https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1017930332101]
4. **Veriserum** (arXiv:2509.05483, https://arxiv.org/html/2509.05483) — expected value: (a) field evidence on the SAME anatomy class (knee-implant projections) that differentiable rendering + a gradient optimizer reaches MAE < 0.8 mm / 0.9° (PyTorch3D + ADAM) — this sets the achievable-precision prior for the arm's pre-registered effect size; (b) their in-plane vs out-of-plane per-DOF error convention (the ablation's per-axis reporting, already adopted round 1); (c) ADAM as the optimizer — relevant because per-axis normalization is exactly what the badly-scaled z axis needs; the MVP's sign-step is the cheap substitute, ADAM is the spec'd upgrade if the sign-step plateaus. Honest caveat to record with the pull: their sub-mm numbers are projection-fitting with known geometry and are in-plane-dominated — the paper supports the in-plane claim, not a single-plane z claim (their own convention separates the axes). Changes: the update rule (sign-step → ADAM-lite) and the effect-size pre-registration; potentially the surrogate (NCC vs chamfer) if the chamfer underperforms. [Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.05483]
5. **SoftRas** (arXiv:1904.01786, https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.01786) + **DIB-R** (arXiv:1908.01210, https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.01210) — expected value: (a) the soft-coverage gradient formulas (SoftRas's temperature-annealed probability field — gradient flows to ALL covering triangles weighted by coverage: the principled fix for the R2-3 last-writer approximation); (b) DIB-R's interpolation-based gradients (the alternative); (c) the benchmark comparisons Modular Primitives reports against them (scoping for the AA increment). Changes: ONLY the fallback list — if the FD-twin check shows the last-writer/overlap error is large, the fix is either the in-stack depth-buffer ownership or a ~50-line SoftRas-style coverage kernel; neither is MVP. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.01786; https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.01210]
6. **DiffDRR** (https://github.com/eigenvivek/DiffDRR) + **DiffPose** (arXiv:2312.06358, https://arxiv.org/html/2312.06358) — expected value: (a) DiffDRR: the DRR-forward gradient machinery — the exact implementation the NO-GO'd photometric route would need, kept on file with its precondition documented (a CT + intensity target, which this stack lacks; a saturated metal implant has no usable intensity gradient in the blob interior — round-1 verdict); (b) DiffPose: 6-DoF pose estimation from DRRs with per-DOF error reporting on real X-ray — the field evidence for the in-plane/out-of-plane split and the single-plane z limitation; (c) both are PyTorch-based — implementation-level evidence FOR the round-1 NO-GO on a torch bridge (their backward is custom autograd over CUDA kernels; torch buys only the wrapper, not the kernels — and the "no torch in the cost path" convention stands; the ATen include at CostFunctionManager.h:28 is the flagged smell, now angle 04's Cut F). Changes: none to the MVP; hardens the photometric NO-GO with implementation references. [Source: https://github.com/eigenvivek/DiffDRR; https://arxiv.org/html/2312.06358; angles/04-backend-architecture.org R2-5]
- Confidence: high on the papers' existence and the mapping of each to a concrete MVP/NO-GO decision; the Veriserum sub-mm claim and the NVDiffrast issue-#70 quote are cited as reported (the #70 page fetch remains incomplete — round-1 note stands).
- Relevance to this project: the user asked for the pull list; each paper now has an explicit "what it changes" — two can change the MVP's math (1906.07870's boundary term, Veriserum's ADAM), one can change the loop design (Gablonsky), and three harden the NO-GO/fallback positions (NVDiffrast AA, SoftRas/DIB-R coverage, DiffDRR/DiffPose photometric).

### What Could Not Be Verified

- The precondition-gate threshold VALUES (G1 ≥ 0.10, G2 ≥ 0.05, G3 ≤ 2 mm) and the actual valley depths: pre-registered hypotheses; the probe has not run. The claim that "at leaf dilation 1 the dilated-overlap is not maximally flat" is derived from the calibration arithmetic (6 mm of z per px of boundary motion) and the EdgeKernel/DilateKernel pixel-flip semantics — the relative valley depths are exactly what the gate measures.
- Whether the boundary term (pixels entering/leaving the EDGE set) is negligible in this geometry: argued (small inside the DIRECT basin) but unmeasured; the FD-twin check is the arbiter and has not run.
- The magnitude of the last-writer attribute error in overlap regions (R2-3's visibility caveat): bounded by the silhouette's overlap fraction, unquantified for the femur STL (the ON-vs-OFF IoU / watertightness checks from angle 02 would inform it; neither has run).
- The real per-axis gap σ across units (the arm's effect-size scale): unmeasured until the first nightly 12-unit run; the power statement is the honest conditional ("conclusive at 1σ, underpowered below").
- The exact boundary-pixel count N_edge (≈ 1200 at r ≈ 200 px is an estimate from the silhouette radius, not a measurement) — it sets the quantization floor used in the h-calibration rule.
- NVDiffrast issue #70 remains search-snippet-verified only (direct fetch failed in round 1); the z/w no-gradient position is consistent with the nvdiffrast docs but should be re-checked against the local Zotero copy when pulled.
- Whether the analytic arm's 500-step cap is reachable within B_p = 1000 at the real wall-clock per step: the ~1 render/step claim is structurally exact (the verification render doubles as the gradient base), but per-eval timing is angle 05's unmeasured datum.
- The dispatch's LOCAL CONTEXT phrase "torch only in ML services" is accurate for the COST PATH (no torch in DIRECT_DILATION or any metric kernel) but not for the link graph (torch is linked into jtml_compute via machine_learning_tools.cpp; the unused ATen include at CostFunctionManager.h:28 is angle 04's Cut F) — noted so the two statements do not collide in synthesis.

### Sources

- repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu + include/compute/render_engine.cuh — WorldToPixelKernel (projection with signed fx/fy, tZ==0 → −1e-6 guard), FillTriangleKernel (unnormalized barycentrics a/b/c/denominator, two-branch inside test, 255 write, fragment-stream binary search), SetPose (R = Rz·Rx·Ry), Render() (2 D2H syncs: bounding box + fragment_fill), InitializeCUDA/FreeCuda (dev_z_line_values_ precedent for the attribute buffer), Pose struct field order. Verified by direct read this round.
- repo — src/compute/gpu_model.cu:115-123 — RenderPrimaryCamera = SetPose + Render; the polish loop's render seam.
- repo — src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu + src/compute/fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu + include/compute/fast_implant_dilation_metric.cuh — the chamfer surrogate (reads EDGE_PIXEL only; int atomicAdd; the :27 index bug to NOT copy; the crop formula), the EdgeKernel dependency (declared in the .cuh, WHITE→EDGE in place, EDGE survives the dilation pass), DilateKernel/DifferenceKernel semantics (DILATED=99 excluded from the chamfer).
- repo — src/compute/DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:73-104 — the production composition (white_sum + FastImplantDilationMetric + DistanceMapMetric at :80; dead duplicate at :101-104).
- repo — test/unit/frame_headless.cpp:129-137 + include/compute/frame.h — SetDistanceMap = OpenCV distanceTransform(DIST_L1, mask 5, CV_8UC1) on the inverted edge image; the distance map is uint8 and truncates at 255.
- repo — include/compute/pixel_grayscale_colors.h:9-12 — WHITE 255 / BLACK 0 / EDGE 100 / DILATED 99 (the EDGE-set non-interference argument).
- repo — include/compute/CostFunctionManager.h:163 — gpu_distance_maps_ = vector<GPUFrame*> (the polish's distance map, never recomputed).
- repo — example_studies/Kneel_1/calibration.txt — JT_INTCALIB: 1198 mm principal distance, 0.373 mm pixel pitch → fx ≈ −3212 px, 1 px = 0.373 mm, boundary motion ≈ r_px·ΔZ/1198 (all step-size defaults derive from these numbers).
- repo — test/golden/baseline.json — 3 Kneel_1 frames, fem.jts golden z per frame (−1027.713 / −1026.732 / −1028.69), IoU 0.85 gate, budget 20/25/30/35k, ranges (leaf 3, leaf_z 15), dilation_px (leaf 1), observed z gap 6.31 mm, JT_EULER_312 pose convention.
- angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org R2-1/R2-2/R2-4 — the z-profile probe spec (31-render ±15 mm sweep, valley_depth formula, z-blind threshold 0.05, pin-first p1-p4), the perturbation suite's Δ set, the ablation.json schema (runs/z_profiles/perturbation_calibration/determinism), the ci/nightly split, the stage-bookkeeping gate.
- https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2011.03277 — Modular Primitives: per-pixel (ID, u, v, zc/wc) + 2×2 barycentric Jacobian; backward ∂L/∂{x_c,y_c,z_c,w_c} = ∂L/∂{u,v}·∂{u,v}/∂{x_c,y_c,z_c,w_c} (Eq. 2) + ∂L/∂J_uv, scatter-add to vertices (re-fetched and re-verified this round). The rigid-body simplification (no J_uv term, no vertex scatter) is the MVP's cost saving vs the reference.
- https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast + https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast/issues/70 — the reference CUDA backward (scatter-add), the analytic AA spec for the fallback list, the z/w no-gradient policy.
- https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.07870 — Analytical Derivatives for Differentiable Renderer: 3D Pose Estimation — the boundary-term treatment and 6-DoF silhouette-gradient protocol the FD-twin check borrows.
- https://repository.lib.ncsu.edu/items/37f7120b-c41e-4267-83d7-5cea4e770b4d + https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1017930332101 — Gablonsky: DIRECT+local-search hybrid theory, STOP/re-seed rules, locally-biased DIRECT (the DIRECT-side upgrade if the arm wins).
- https://arxiv.org/html/2509.05483 — Veriserum: knee-implant differentiable-registration evidence (MAE < 0.8 mm / 0.9°, ADAM, in-plane/out-of-plane convention) — the effect-size prior and the ADAM upgrade path.
- https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.01786 + https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.01210 — SoftRas / DIB-R: soft-coverage fallback formulas (the fix for the last-writer approximation if the twin check shows it matters).
- https://github.com/eigenvivek/DiffDRR + https://arxiv.org/html/2312.06358 — the DRR-gradient machinery and 6-DoF-DRR pose evidence; hardens the photometric NO-GO and the torch-bridge NO-GO.
- repo — example_studies/Subject0 (Cam1/Cam2 biplane, STLs) — the future frame pool, out of MVP scope (different fixtures/calibration).

PASS = per-axis |g_a − g_fd| ≤ 0.5·|g_fd| + floor with matching signs; FAIL = record, fall back to FD for the rest of the run, and file the analytic-kernel bug (candidate causes, in order: last-writer attribute mismatch in overlap regions; the omitted boundary term — pixels entering/leaving the EDGE set; ∇D convention at the crop border). This is the empirical gate that decides whether the boundary term (the one approximate piece of the math) is negligible in THIS geometry — it is verified, not assumed, and it is exactly what arXiv:1906.07870's treatment would formalize if it is not (R2-6). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.07870; angle 06 Round 1 "smooth surrogate" (boundary-term discussion)]
- Cost per step (analytic arm): 1 render/step — the acceptance verification render at θ_k is the base for the gradient kernel (FastImplantDilationMetric edge-marks it, the chamfer value call reads it, the gradient kernel reads it after — all on the same image state; EDGE pixels survive the dilation pass, R2-1); then θ_{k+1} = clamp(θ_k − α·h·sign(g), leaf_box) with the same α-halving acceptance rule. At B_p = 1000: ~800 accepted steps, capped by polish_max_steps = 500 (default) → the analytic arm usually stops on the cap or the α-exhaustion stall, whichever first; the evals actually used are recorded. [Source: angle 06 Round 1 "hybrid loop" + "feasibility verdicts" (1 render/step, +1 week)]
- Confidence: high on the math and kernel structure (every formula traces to verified code); medium on the boundary-term magnitude and the overlap-fraction error until the twin check runs (they are measurements by design).
- Relevance to this project: this is the +1-week analytic increment over the FD MVP, with its own falsifiable gate (the twin check) and its own determinism requirement (the ordered reduction — a requirement that only becomes visible when you trace the polish through the ablation runner's rerun_identical assertion).

#### R2-5 — The ablation arm that arbitrates contradiction 6: THREE arms at equal cumulative budget, the B-arm budget-gift control, the IoU gate, per-axis gaps, and the sample size that makes it conclusive
- The round-1 two-arm design had a confound this round's redesign removes: DIRECT-only@B vs DIRECT@(B−B_p)+polish@B_p cannot separate "polish added quality" from "the 1000 evals were spent better by polish than DIRECT would have spent them" — the budget gift itself is the alternative explanation. The pre-registered design is therefore three arms, all from the same start seed, all on the same frame:
  - **A: DIRECT-only@35k** (production shape 20/25/30/35k) — the reference.
  - **B: DIRECT-only@34k** (leaf 5000→4000; cumulative 20/25/30/34k) — the budget-gift control: it is what DIRECT does with the budget BEFORE the polish gets it.
  - **C: DIRECT@34k + polish@B_p = 1000** (DIRECT as in B, then RunPolishStage at the leaf optimum; polish evals push the counter to 35k).
  C wins only if C beats B (polish used its 1000 evals better than DIRECT would have — the marginal-value test) AND C ≥ A (no net loss at equal total budget — the equal-budget test). If C > B but C < A, polish added nothing net: the 1000 evals were better spent by DIRECT. This is the honest arbitrage of the "12x" thesis: at FIXED total budget the thesis reduces to a final-quality comparison; the "fewer evals" reading only materializes when the DIRECT budget itself shrinks (the ML-initializer pathway), which the arm records but does not claim. [Source: angle 06 Round 1 "12x thesis"; synthesis Contradiction 6; repo — test/golden/baseline.json budget_per_stage]
- Budget bookkeeping (round-1 rule, made exact): every polish surrogate eval AND every trial verification increments cost_function_calls_, so C's counter lands on 20/25/30/34k during DIRECT and 35k after polish; the stage-bookkeeping gate (angle 03: costCalls() on the cumulative caps) applies to A/B/C identically. Surrogate evals are counted at parity with production evals — conservative FOR polish (a surrogate eval is cheaper: ~5 launches + 2 syncs vs ~15 launches + 5 syncs), so a win under parity accounting is a win a fortiori; a time-based variant is a recorded follow-up, not an MVP claim. [Source: angle 06 Round 1 "budget semantics"; angles/05-compute-perf.org sync inventory]
- Gates and recordings (per unit, per arm): the IoU ≥ 0.85 appearance gate on the ORACLE renderer (backface OFF — the same comparator as DIRECT-only's final measurement, so the two arms are never compared through different conventions; baseline.json silhouette_iou_threshold 0.85); per-px L1 banded-record; per-axis pose gaps vs fem.jts (pose_gap_vs_golden_mm_deg — the schema field angle 03 already defines); z-gap banded-informational; final production cost; evals-to-gate via a data profile (IoU sampled at 1k-eval checkpoints — 35 extra renders per run, trivial; C's verification evals give a dense profile for the final 1000). ablation.json gains a polish block: {arm, surrogate: "DistanceMapMetric", gradient: "forward-difference|analytic", steps, evals_used, final_production_cost, h: [6], alpha_halvings, per_axis_gap_mm_deg, iou, z_gap_mm, precondition: {g1..g4: bool}, determinism: {run_hash, rerun_identical}} and the z_profiles records gain a term field {term: "full|chamfer|dilated"}. [Source: angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org R2-2 + R2-4 (schema); repo — test/golden/baseline.json tolerances]
- Sample size and what is conclusive (honest power math): the sampling unit is (frame × start seed) — DIRECT is deterministic per seed (RNG-free bookkeeping), and the polish is deterministic given the ordered-reduction gradient (R2-4), so the per-unit variance is entirely across units, and the design is paired (A/B/C from the same seed). For a paired one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank, α = 0.05, power 0.8: detecting a 1σ improvement needs N ≈ 12 pairs; detecting 0.5σ needs N ≈ 34. The in-repo pool is Kneel_1's 3 frames (baseline.json expected_pose_per_frame × 3) — so the pre-registered unit construction is 3 frames × 4 start seeds = 12 units (seeds: truth + one in-plane x, one in-plane y, one z perturbation chosen from the perturbation suite's Δ set, e.g. ±2 mm / +5 mm z — pre-registered in the manifest), which is **conclusive at 1σ effects and honestly underpowered below that** (the arm reports the achieved power; a 0.5σ outcome is recorded as "inconclusive", not as a null). σ is estimated from the per-axis gap distribution across the 12 DIRECT-only units after the first nightly run. Subject0 (example_studies/Subject0, Cam1/Cam2 biplane with STLs) is a future frame pool only — different fixtures/calibration, out of scope for the MVP arm. Cost: 12 units × 3 arms × ~15 min (35k shape at the verified 20-60 evals/s) ≈ 9 h on the 3090 → the full matrix is nightly; CI runs 1 frame × 3 arms on the Moré & Wild reduced shape. [Source: repo — test/golden/baseline.json (3 frames, budget), example_studies/{Kneel_1,Subject0}; angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org R2-1 (perturbation Δ set) + R2-4 (ci/nightly split)]
- The landing rule (round-1, made operational): polish ships behind enable_polish_/polish_budget_/polish_max_steps only when, over the 12-unit matrix: (a) the IoU ≥ 0.85 gate passes on every unit in every arm; (b) C beats B on median final production cost AND median in-plane gap (paired test at the pre-registered effect size); (c) C ≥ A on the same (no net loss at equal budget); (d) no per-axis gap regression beyond the minimal-detectable-regression table (the perturbation suite's deliverable — a regression the gate can see is a fail by definition); (e) the precondition gate (R2-1) recorded, and any z-gap claim is made only if G1-G4 held. The "12x fewer evals" figure is recorded as a target, not a justification, and is structurally capped at the leaf-phase win (round-1 analysis stands). [Source: angle 06 Round 1 "Recommended go/no-go"; synthesis Contradiction 6]
- Confidence: high on the mechanics (seams, schema, budget shape all source-verified; the B-arm confound is a design argument); medium on the effect-size pre-registration (σ is unmeasured until the first nightly run — reported, not assumed).
- Relevance to this project: this is the instrument that closes the run's only explicitly low-confidence claim (Contradiction 6) with a design that cannot mistake a budget gift for a polish win — and it plugs into angle 03's runner with a schema extension, not new infrastructure.

#### R2-6 — Zotero pull list with per-paper expected value: what each paper changes about the MVP or the NO-GO list
1. **NVDiffrast** (nvlabs/nvdiffrast, https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast) — expected value: (a) the reference CUDA backward kernel shapes — their rasterize_bwd is a scatter-add over triangle IDs, the exact accumulation pattern the MVP's gradient kernel uses, confirming the design before it is written; (b) the attribute-gradient chain incl. the 2×2 barycentric Jacobian (Eq. 2 in Modular Primitives) — which the MVP does NOT need for a rigid body (R2-3), so the paper's highest value here is the *negative*: it shows exactly what the MVP saves; (c) the analytic post-process AA implementation = the concrete spec for the boundary-term correction IF the FD-twin check shows the term is non-negligible; (d) the z/w no-gradient policy (issue #70, search-verified round 1) — reconfirms NDC-depth stays off the polish path. Changes to the MVP: none required; upgrades the fallback list with a copyable AA spec. [Source: https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast, https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast/issues/70, https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2011.03277]
2. **"Analytical Derivatives for Differentiable Renderer: 3D Pose Estimation"** (arXiv:1906.07870, https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.07870) — expected value: (a) the boundary-term derivation (pixels entering/leaving the rendered region under pose perturbation) — the ONE piece of the MVP math that is approximate, and the paper is the closest published treatment of exactly this discrete-sampling derivative; (b) their 6-DoF pose-estimation protocol from silhouette gradients — a ready-made validation recipe the FD-twin check borrows; (c) their edge-pixel-only summation (same as the MVP's EDGE-set sum). Changes: decides whether the analytic kernel needs a ~20-line boundary-term addition; if yes, supplies the exact term. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.07870]
3. **Gablonsky's thesis + "A Locally-Biased form of the DIRECT Algorithm"** (https://repository.lib.ncsu.edu/items/37f7120b-c41e-4267-83d7-5cea4e770b4d; DOI 10.1023/A:1017930332101) — expected value: (a) the DIRECT+local-search hybrid's termination theory — the polish's STOP rule (production-cost stall over N steps + α-exhaustion) gets a literature-anchored justification; (b) the locally-biased DIRECT algorithm itself — the DIRECT-side upgrade that makes the hybrid self-consistent IF the arm wins (bias selection toward the current optimum; related to but distinct from angle 01's -gb refinement); (c) their test methodology — a battery protocol angle 01's analytic battery can reuse for the polish surrogate. Changes: the STOP/re-seed loop design; nothing to the kernels. [Source: https://repository.lib.ncsu.edu/items/37f7120b-c41e-4267-83d7-5cea4e770b4d; https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1017930332101]
4. **Veriserum** (arXiv:2509.05483, https://arxiv.org/html/2509.05483) — expected value: (a) field evidence on the SAME anatomy class (knee-implant projections) that differentiable rendering + a gradient optimizer reaches MAE < 0.8 mm / 0.9° (PyTorch3D + ADAM) — this sets the achievable-precision prior for the arm's pre-registered effect size; (b) their in-plane vs out-of-plane per-DOF error convention (the ablation's per-axis reporting, already adopted round 1); (c) ADAM as the optimizer — relevant because per-axis normalization is exactly what the badly-scaled z axis needs; the MVP's sign-step is the cheap substitute, ADAM is the spec'd upgrade if the sign-step plateaus. Honest caveat to record with the pull: their sub-mm numbers are projection-fitting with known geometry and are in-plane-dominated — the paper supports the in-plane claim, not a single-plane z claim (their own convention separates the axes). Changes: the update rule (sign-step → ADAM-lite) and the effect-size pre-registration; potentially the surrogate (NCC vs chamfer) if the chamfer underperforms. [Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.05483]
5. **SoftRas** (arXiv:1904.01786, https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.01786) + **DIB-R** (arXiv:1908.01210, https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.01210) — expected value: (a) the soft-coverage gradient formulas (SoftRas's temperature-annealed probability field — gradient flows to ALL covering triangles weighted by coverage: the principled fix for the R2-3 last-writer approximation); (b) DIB-R's interpolation-based gradients (the alternative); (c) the benchmark comparisons Modular Primitives reports against them (scoping for the AA increment). Changes: ONLY the fallback list — if the FD-twin check shows the last-writer/overlap error is large, the fix is either the in-stack depth-buffer ownership or a ~50-line SoftRas-style coverage kernel; neither is MVP. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.01786; https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.01210]
6. **DiffDRR** (https://github.com/eigenvivek/DiffDRR) + **DiffPose** (arXiv:2312.06358, https://arxiv.org/html/2312.06358) — expected value: (a) DiffDRR: the DRR-forward gradient machinery — the exact implementation the NO-GO'd photometric route would need, kept on file with its precondition documented (a CT + intensity target, which this stack lacks; a saturated metal implant has no usable intensity gradient in the blob interior — round-1 verdict); (b) DiffPose: 6-DoF pose estimation from DRRs with per-DOF error reporting on real X-ray — the field evidence for the in-plane/out-of-plane split and the single-plane z limitation; (c) both are PyTorch-based — implementation-level evidence FOR the round-1 NO-GO on a torch bridge (their backward is custom autograd over CUDA kernels; torch buys only the wrapper, not the kernels — and the "no torch in the cost path" convention stands; the ATen include at CostFunctionManager.h:28 is the flagged smell, now angle 04's Cut F). Changes: none to the MVP; hardens the photometric NO-GO with implementation references. [Source: https://github.com/eigenvivek/DiffDRR; https://arxiv.org/html/2312.06358; angles/04-backend-architecture.org R2-5]
- Confidence: high on the papers' existence and the mapping of each to a concrete MVP/NO-GO decision; the Veriserum sub-mm claim and the NVDiffrast issue-#70 quote are cited as reported (the #70 page fetch remains incomplete — round-1 note stands).
- Relevance to this project: the user asked for the pull list; each paper now has an explicit "what it changes" — two can change the MVP's math (1906.07870's boundary term, Veriserum's ADAM), one can change the loop design (Gablonsky), and three harden the NO-GO/fallback positions (NVDiffrast AA, SoftRas/DIB-R coverage, DiffDRR/DiffPose photometric).

### What Could Not Be Verified

- The precondition-gate threshold VALUES (G1 ≥ 0.10, G2 ≥ 0.05, G3 ≤ 2 mm) and the actual valley depths: pre-registered hypotheses; the probe has not run. The claim that "at leaf dilation 1 the dilated-overlap is not maximally flat" is derived from the calibration arithmetic (6 mm of z per px of boundary motion) and the EdgeKernel/DilateKernel pixel-flip semantics — the relative valley depths are exactly what the gate measures.

#+TITLE: Panoptes Research: Optimizer Deep-Dive — Architecture + Algorithm Upgrades
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+RESEARCH_ANGLES: 6
#+ROUND: 3 (wave 1 complete) — angles 01–04 carry '## Round 3' sections grounded in Zotero primary texts; angles 05–06 remain round-2 complete (rounds: 1 = all six; 2 wave 1 = 01–04; 2 wave 2 = 05–06; 3 wave 1 = 01–04)
#+STATUS: complete

* Executive Summary

The single highest-leverage finding of this run: **the current 0.9936 IoU baseline is measured against a deterministically-corrupted cost term.** Angle 02 verified at the dispatch's line numbers that the distance-map index formula (distance_map_metric.cu:27, `blockIdx.y + gridDim.x` instead of `blockIdx.y * gridDim.x`) mis-maps every block row, so the distance-map term of every DIRECT_DILATION oracle evaluation accumulates at the wrong pixels. That is the one live bug of the seven verified — the other six poison latent paths only. Fixing it and re-baselining (one single re-baseline after all behavior-neutral fixes land) is the prerequisite for every other decision in this run: variant switches, perf cuts, and gradient polish are all judged against a baseline that is not trustworthy until this lands. The gate (IoU ≥ 0.85) is far below the measured 0.9936, so the appearance arbiter stays, but measured IoU / per-px L1 / the 6.31 mm z gap are informational and expected to move.

Round 2 sharpened the critical path in an important way: the corrupted index has **exactly one reader** (DistanceMapMetric_Kernel, invoked only from DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:80), and every post-optimize measurement metric (IoU, per-px L1, chamfer) uses the correct formula — so the 0.9936/0.0207 numbers themselves are not corrupted, only the cost that drove the search. The corruption is a systematic exclusion: the top ~64 crop rows of the rendered band are never sampled and the middle band is multiplicity-over-weighted, so the distance-map term is *flatter in z* than the honest chamfer complement. The structural prediction is that the re-baselined DIRECT optimum moves toward the golden z and the frame-1 6.31 mm z gap shrinks materially (direction: medium-high confidence; magnitude: not predictable without the GPU re-run).

Round 2 wave 2 added two more high-value deliverables on top of the wave-1 deepening. **First, the ms/call meter carries a 1000× unit error on Linux, on top of its CPU-time blind spot**: grep finds zero CLOCKS_PER_SEC anywhere in src/ — both meter sites (optimizer_manager.cpp:1197-1203 end-of-frame and :1272-1279 iteration callback) divide raw clock() ticks by calls and label the result "ms/call"; on Linux glibc clock() returns microseconds, so the value is CPU-µs/call labeled as ms/call. The UI compounds it: "Iterations Per Second: 1000.0 / iteration_speed" (mainscreen.cpp:4654-4655) reads the µs value as ms → IPS understated ~1000×, and the ETA (:4598/:4659) is overstated by the same factor. This is a correctness fact, not polish — no before/after perf claim through the existing meter is meaningful, and Cut 4 (now a full spec for BOTH sites) must emit true ms/call so the existing UI math becomes correct without UI changes. [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org R2-1/R2-2] **Second, the polish stage is now an executable MVP spec with its own falsifiable preconditions**: a term-decomposed z-profile probe (chamfer-only vs dilated-overlap-only valley depths from the same 31 renders, pre-registered thresholds G1–G4 at leaf dilation 1), a forward-difference arm (7 renders/accepted step, ~140 steps within B_p = 1000), an analytic arm (1 render/step via the 2×6 projection Jacobian + gradient-of-distance-map kernel, with an ordered two-pass float reduction so the ablation runner's rerun_identical determinism twin cannot trip), and a **three-arm study (A: DIRECT@35k, B: DIRECT@34k budget-gift control, C: DIRECT@34k + polish@1000)** that arbitrates the 12x-vs-1.5–3x contradiction without confounding "polish quality" with "budget reallocation". [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org R2-1/R2-2/R2-4/R2-5]

Round 3 (wave 1) moved the run's evidentiary base onto the primary texts: angles 01–04 re-verified their round-1/2 conclusions against the Zotero corpus (Flood 2018, Mahfouz 2003, Jones 1993, Gablonsky 2001, Jensen 2024, Yamazaki 2004, the DIRECTGO / DIRECT-GLh / 2022-study papers, Burton, Arulampalam) and **resolved three open contradictions outright**. (1) **Mahfouz normalization**: the paper corroborates the kernel's structure (two predicted-sum-normalized ratios, contour weighted more heavily, negative weights, a 3-px capture band — a full lineage match) but the numeric weights are unextractable (embedded PDF equations), so the kernel-as-spec verdict keeps 2.55/×255/−2.67/−1 and only the pointer-guard fix proceeds. (2) **Three-way dilation contradiction**: Flood's constants are now verbatim — femur 10/6/1, tibia 6/2/1, branch = trunk−4, leaf = 1; leaf=1 is unanimous, trunk 6 (code AND docs) is the paper's TIBIA value applied to a FEMUR (femur robust band 8–12), and BOTH 6/4/1 and 6/3/1 violate branch=trunk−4 — so the dilation-schedule ablation now tests the lineage configs {10,6,1}, {6,2,1}, {6,4,1}, {6,3,1} plus a bilateral-vs-render-only semantics axis. (3) **GLh formula**: verified from the paper itself (raw surrogate f_min + d stored, selection-time normalized d̃ = d/√n with f̃_min ≡ 0, f̃=1 flat case, 1e-6 recompute threshold, Definition-1 feasibility detection) with a ready-made constrained battery (Emmental-GKLS, 100/100 solved by GLh in the paper). One description-level correction matters for every downstream number: **the oracle's DIRECT_DILATION cost chases the dilated Canny edges of the fluoroscopy frame, not the Study2Grid label — only the IoU/L1 gate uses the label** — so the Canny config (oracle 3/0/150 vs production 3/40/120 vs paper femur-A 3/30/80) is cost-load-bearing, and the Phase-2 re-baseline must stay single-variable (index fix only). [Sources: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org R3-1/R3-2/R3-3/R3-5; angles/01-direct-variants.org R3-1]

The recommended course of action, in dependency order, is unchanged in shape and now fully specified in content, with the Round-3 deltas folded in: (1) pin-first fixes per angle 02 (Tier-0 pins, behavior-neutral fixes, the distance-map index fix + one oracle re-baseline — plus the CUDA-free finite-check at DirectOptimizer::EvaluateCostFunction, needed regardless of GLh; * Executive Summary

The single highest-leverage finding of this run: **the current 0.9936 IoU baseline is measured against a deterministically-corrupted cost term.** Angle 02 verified at the dispatch's line numbers that the distance-map index formula (distance_map_metric.cu:27, `blockIdx.y + gridDim.x` instead of `blockIdx.y * gridDim.x`) mis-maps every block row, so the distance-map term of every DIRECT_DILATION oracle evaluation accumulates at the wrong pixels. That is the one live bug of the seven verified — the other six poison latent paths only. Fixing it and re-baselining (one single re-baseline after all behavior-neutral fixes land) is the prerequisite for every other decision in this run: variant switches, perf cuts, and gradient polish are all judged against a baseline that is not trustworthy until this lands. The gate (IoU ≥ 0.85) is far below the measured 0.9936, so the appearance arbiter stays, but measured IoU / per-px L1 / the 6.31 mm z gap are informational and expected to move.

Round 2 sharpened the critical path in an important way: the corrupted index has **exactly one reader** (DistanceMapMetric_Kernel, invoked only from DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:80), and every post-optimize measurement metric (IoU, per-px L1, chamfer) uses the correct formula — so the 0.9936/0.0207 numbers themselves are not corrupted, only the cost that drove the search. Now, the zotero_rag_query tool isn't in my function list, so I'll read the corpus files directly. Let me start reading the key papers. Given file sizes, I'll read strategically — grep for key terms, then read relevant sections.

Let me plan the research:

**(1) THE CORPUS SURVEY** — which gradient strategy is cheapest to implement against JTML's hand-written CUDA silhouette rasterizer:
- SoftRas (liuSoftRasterizerDifferentiable2019): soft coverage — probabilistic rasterization. Requires per-pixel coverage probabilities from all triangles; expensive; would require reworking the rasterizer to accumulate per-triangle coverage with temperature. Cost: high.
- Modular Primitives (laineModularPrimitivesHighPerformance2020): already covered in round 1/2 — (ID, u, v, zc/wc) + barycentric Jacobian; vertex-position gradients. For rigid body, simplified. Already in-corpus now, so I can verify the round-1 claims against the primary text.
- zhangPathspaceDifferentiableRendering2020: path-space differentiable rendering — for global illumination, radiance; not relevant to silhouette registration of an implant (X-ray). Probably a NO-GO / not-applicable to this problem.
- mehtaTheoryTopologicalDerivatives2023: topological derivatives for differentiable rendering — handles visibility discontinuities by sampling boundary crossings in continuous space. This is relevant to the "boundary term" question in R2-4! Their approach: separate the integral into smooth regions and boundary terms, sample points near the boundary (edge sampling). This is a cheap-ish alternative: instead of the analytic boundary term, sample silhouette boundary points. Actually the paper is about a theory of topological derivatives and gives a practical algorithm with edge sampling. This could inform the boundary-term question.
- nicoletLargeStepsInverse2021: "Large Steps in Inverse Rendering of Geometry" — uses silhouette rasterization? Let me read. I recall it proposes a regularized differentiable renderer with a distance-based loss; key idea: optimize geometry with large steps using SDF-like or mesh-based approaches... Actually "Large Steps" introduces a differentiable renderer that computes gradients through a signed distance approximation and a "warp" to allow large steps. It uses triangle rendering with a smooth approximation of the binary visibility. This is very relevant: it's about avoiding local minima and taking large steps in inverse rendering, using a *smoothed* silhouette.
- wangSimpleApproachDifferentiable2024: "A Simple Approach to Differentiable Rendering" — I believe this is the "edge sampling via line integrals / differentiable soft rasterizer without per-triangle probabilities"? Let me read it. Actually I recall "A Simple Approach for Differentiable Rendering" (Wang, ?) — it proposes a simple way: render with a 1-px dilation, compute gradients w.r.t. vertices via the antialiased coverage difference. Let me read the actual text.
- bangaruDifferentiableRenderingNeural2022: "Differentiable Rendering of Neural SDFs through Reparameterization" — SDF reparameterization: gradients through ray-marched neural SDFs via reparameterization. For JTML: the implant is an STL mesh, not a neural SDF. Relevance: the reparameterization idea (smooth gradient via sampling the surface) could apply, but building an SDF from the STL is extra machinery. Probably NOT the cheapest.
- gopalakrishnanFastAutoDifferentiableDigitally2022: DiffDRR — auto-differentiable DRR. PyTorch-based; DRR forward model with rotation/translation and a cone-beam projector (siddon). This is the DRR family — the question: does it change the 'no torch in the cost path' boundary? DiffDRR's projector is a custom CUDA kernel via PyTorch autograd (they wrote a custom op). The paper shows a "fast" implementation in pure PyTorch vs a CUDA op. Relevance: it demonstrates that a torch-free CUDA core with a thin autograd binding is feasible; but for JTML the answer remains: torch adds nothing for 6-DoF rigid pose of a static STL. But the DiffDRR family DOES change one thing: it provides a cheap, testable reference implementation of the DRR-forward + analytic Jacobian for the *z-line-integral* channel (the ML pathway), and gopalakrishnan et al. have the "Fast, auto-differentiable digitally reconstructed radiographs" (DiffDRR) paper with a differentiable projector that could serve as an *oracle/reference* for a hand-written CUDA forward projector. Also important: DiffDRR's z-line-integral channel is the stronger z signal (round 1 said so).
- kimDifferentiableForwardProjector2023: LEAP — torch-free C++/CUDA core behind a thin torch.nn.Module binding, XCT volume line integrals. Already cited in angle 04 R3-4 (matched-projector doctrine). In-corpus now; I can verify.

**(2) THE SIMPLEX PRECEDENT** — Mahfouz 2003 used SA-modified Nelder-Mead simplex with negative weights for this exact registration. The repo deliberately diverged from SA ("Not Using Simulated Annealing Obviously..."). Re-evaluate: the polish MVP's gradient choice vs a cheap simplex-polish alternative. The ablation arm should include a simplex arm if the surrogate valley is shallow. Nelder-Mead on a 6-DoF pose with chamfer surrogate: ~7 evals per iteration (one per vertex), no gradient needed, works on noisy/quantized costs. It's a derivative-free pattern search; for the chamfer surrogate (which is smooth-ish), NM converges linearly. The cost: ~1 render per eval. A Robust Method for Registration of
Three-Dimensional Knee Implant Models to
Two-Dimensional Fluoroscopy Images
Mohamed R. Mahfouz*, William A. Hoff, Richard D. Komistek, and Douglas A. Dennis

Abstract—A method was developed for registering three-dimensional knee implant models to single plane X-ray fluoroscopy images. We use a direct image-to-image similarity measure, taking
advantage of the speed of modern computer graphics workstations
to quickly render simulated (predicted) images. As a result, the
method does not require an accurate segmentation of the implant
silhouette in the image (which can be prone to errors). A robust
optimization algorithm (simulated annealing) is used that can escape local minima and find the global minimum (true solution). Although we focus on the analysis of total knee arthroplasty (TKA)
in this paper, the method can be (and has been) applied to other
implanted joints, including, but not limited to, hips, ankles, and
temporomandibular joints. Convergence tests on an in vivo image
show that the registration method can reliably find poses that are
very close to the optimal (i.e., within 0.4 and 0.1 mm), even from
starting poses with large initial errors. However, the precision of
translation measurement in the
(out-of-plane) direction is not
as good. We also show that the method is robust with respect to
image noise and occlusions. However, a small amount of user supervision and intervention is necessary to detect cases when the
optimization algorithm falls into a local minimum. Intervention is
required less than 5% of the time when the initial starting pose
is reasonably close to the correct answer, but up to 50% of the
time when the initial starting pose is far away. Finally, extensive
evaluations were performed on cadaver images to determine accuracy of relative pose measurement. Comparing against data derived from an optical sensor as a “gold standard,” the overall rootmean-square error of the registration method was approximately
1.5 and 0.65 mm (although translation error was higher). However, uncertainty in the optical sensor data may account for a large
part of the observed error.

content.thinking:
Excellent — very rich primary-text material from Mahfouz 2003. Key facts:

1. The optimizer: "Our SA algorithm is a modified version of the Nelder–Mead [30] (downhill simplex) optimization method. A simplex is a set of seven points where each point represents a possible pose" — 7-point simplex (6-DoF + 1). Iteratively perturbs the worst (highest) point in the direction of a lower score.
2. Simulated annealing: adds/subtracts a positive, logarithmically distributed random variable proportional to temperature to function values in the simplex; temperature decreased every 40 iterations by ×0.99; periodically the simplex is expanded to test more distant solutions.
3. Termination: difference between best and worst points < small threshold.
4. Speed: one iteration ~0.2 s on a Silicon Graphics Octane workstation (1998-era!). That's ~5 evals/s on a 1998 SGI. Compare with JTML's 20-60 evals/s on a 3090.
5. T=0 control: "with temperature equal to zero, the algorithm becomes a simple gradient descent algorithm that just traverses downhill to the nearest local minimum. We found, as expected, that the algorithm quickly fell into a local minimum near its starting point. Thus, the algorithm did not improve the initial pose estimate significantly." — This is DIRECTLY relevant to the polish question: pure local refinement from a far start doesn't help; but the polish starts from the DIRECT leaf optimum (already near the basin), so this T=0 finding is about global search, not polish.
6. "A local search algorithm such as Levenberg–Marquardt will simply find the nearest local minimum" — and the reason they went robust.
7. Future research: "using a more efficient optimization algorithm than simulated annealing" — the paper itself calls for a more efficient optimizer (this is the DIRECT-JTA lineage's own gap).
8. Precision: "within 0.4 and 0.1 mm" — wait, that's "poses that are very close to the optimal (i.e., within 0.4 and 0.1 mm)" — probably 0.4 mm and 0.1°? The abstract says "within 0.4 and 0.1 mm". Hmm, rotation in mm? Actually likely "0.4 mm translation and 0.1 degree rotation"? Let me check the convergence test section around line 560-620.
9. Weights: fixed weights, suggested dynamic adjustment by contrast — relevant to the polish surrogate's fixed SAME_Z weight discussion! "the relative weights in our matching score function (giving the relative importance of the region score versus the contour score) have fixed values, regardless of the object-to-background contrast... It is possible that better performance could be achieved by dynamically adjusting the weights depending on the image contrast." — parallels Yamazaki's "difficult to determine a fixed weight" for z.
10. Chamfer matching reference [28]: "Registration of contours using chamfer matching", Van Herk — the distance-map/chamfer surrogate lineage! The chamfer surrogate is literally the classic Van Herk chamfer matching. Also relevant: the "3 pixels" capture band.

Let me now read the convergence test section (lines ~530-700) to get the out-of-plane precision numbers and the starting pose classes. Let me also check the "sensitivity to z" discussion. And the accuracy of the out-of-plane direction ("However, the precision of translation measurement in the (out-of-plane) direction is not as good").

efficient to use an interactive approach. In this approach, if the
system gets stuck in an incorrect pose, the user can temporarily
seize control of the model (using the mouse) and move it toward
the correct pose. Releasing the mouse then allows the optimization algorithm to resume at the new pose. This initializes the
state vector closer to the solution, saving time by reducing the
number of iterations needed to be performed.
This approach is a form of traded control [32], which is used
in supervised robot control. The philosophy is that the system
incorporates the best of both approaches. It combines the speed
and precision of the computer with the common sense and domain knowledge of the human. The resulting system is both efficient and reliable.
Often the user can easily detect that the system has found a
local minimum (incorrect solution), because the overlay of the
model does not fit the silhouette in the image. In other cases,
the user can see that the resulting femur-tibia pose is physically
