arguments.content:
## Round 3 — The corpus survey, the simplex precedent, and the Yamazaki z-polish (final deepening)

### Summary

This round moved the polish MVP's evidence base onto the in-library primary texts and changed two design decisions. (1) The corpus survey ranks the five dispatch-named gradient strategies against JTML's hand-written CUDA rasterizer: the analytic edge-pixel gradient (the R2-4 design) is confirmed the cheapest — Modular Primitives (now in-corpus) is literally a rasterizer + pixel-dense scatter-add backward, of which the MVP is the rigid-body reduction — while SoftRas coverage, SDF reparameterization, path-space edge sampling, and topological derivatives are more expensive or N/A for a fixed-STL 6-DoF pose; the DiffDRR family does NOT change the 'no torch in the cost path' boundary (DiffDRR exists precisely because low-level CUDA generators lack gradients — the analytic Jacobian is the low-level answer; LEAP documents the CUDA-core-plus-thin-binding pattern JTML already matches). (2) The simplex precedent is real and the MVP design changes: Mahfouz 2003's optimizer IS a 7-point Nelder-Mead simplex with SA temperature (the repo dropped the SA; the simplex remains the cheapest polish of all), and DiffDRR's paper documents Nelder-Mead as the community-standard DRR optimizer — so the R2-5 three-arm study gains a FOURTH arm D (plain Nelder-Mead simplex polish on the chamfer surrogate, B_p = 1000, zero gradient machinery), and C-vs-D at equal polish budget becomes the cleanest isolate of the gradient's marginal value. (3) Yamazaki 2004 is geometry/curve-fit, not gradient-type: a decoupled order-4 polynomial fit over 10 depth samples along the focus→COG ray — confirming the z-depth-channel NO-GO from inside the field's own dedicated-depth paper (no depth channel anywhere; z is purely silhouette-scale) and upgrading the polish's z-arm to the decoupled Yamazaki-style fit as a terminal stage, with the focus→COG ray direction and the jagged-z-curve prior folded into the G1–G4 gate design. (4) The round-2 pull list re-ranks: SoftRas, Modular Primitives, DiffDRR, LEAP, and Gablonsky 2001 are now in-library (superseded as pulls); only arXiv:1906.07870, Veriserum, and the NVDiffrast GitHub repo remain necessary pulls.

### Key Findings

#### R3-1 — The corpus survey: the analytic edge-pixel gradient is the cheapest strategy; the reference implementation is in-library and two round-1/2 open items are resolved
- The R2-3/R2-4 design verified against the primary text (laineModularPrimitivesHighPerformance2020.txt): the rasterizer forward outputs "a 2D sample grid, with each position storing a tuple (ID, u, v, zc/wc)" (L549-552) plus "a buffer with the 2×2 Jacobian of the barycentrics w.r.t. the screen coordinates Juv = ∂{u,v}/∂{x,y}" (L561-562); the backward is "a dense operation over output pixels, using a scatter-add operation to accumulate the gradients from the pixels to the correct vertices based on the triangle IDs" (L589-594); analytic AA is a SEPARATE post-shading stage — "point-sampled visibility causes aliasing at visibility discontinuities, and more crucially, cannot produce visibility-related gradients for vertex positions. Antialiasing converts the discontinuities to smooth changes, from which the gradients can be computed" (L751-762) — exactly the R2-4 structure (pixel-grid kernel + ordered reduction + the AA fallback if the FD-twin gate says the boundary term matters). [Source: corpus — l/laineModularPrimitivesHighPerformance2020.txt]
- RESOLVED (round-1/2 open item): the z/w no-gradient policy is IN THE PAPER, not only in GitHub issue #70: "The NDC depth is utilized only by the subsequent antialiasing module, and does not propagate gradients" (L558-560). The round-1 "issue #70 search-verified only" caveat is closed by the primary text; the GitHub issue retains only verbatim-issue-text value. [Source: corpus — l/laineModularPrimitivesHighPerformance2020.txt L558-560]
- RESOLVED (round-1 open item): the "visibility gradients work at 4x4" phrase is a tiny-image-resolution stress test, not a tile size: "To our surprise, the optimization succeeds even at 4×4 resolution, where the average size of a rendered triangle is approximately half a pixel" (L920-924); at 2×2 "the optimization fails to converge" (L903-904). The claim was about the pipeline surviving sub-pixel triangle sizes — the round-1 "could not be verified" item is now closed against the primary text. [Source: corpus — l/laineModularPrimitivesHighPerformance2020.txt L903-904, L920-924]
- Ranking of the five dispatch-named strategies by implementation cost against the JTML rasterizer (cheapest first): (1) analytic edge-pixel gradient (Modular-Primitives-style, rigid-body reduction) — reuses the fill's computed-and-discarded barycentrics + static dev_triangles_; only the ~10-line staged-attributes sibling kernel + ~50-line ChamferGradientKernel; forward-image semantics untouched. (2) forward-projection / differentiable-DRR (DiffDRR/LEAP family) — the forward model exists (render_drr_engine.cu z-line-integral), but it is the ML-pathway channel, gated by the round-1 photometric NO-GO (saturated metal implant → no usable intensity gradient); not a polish strategy. (3) soft-rasterizer coverage (SoftRas) — per-triangle probabilistic coverage + depth-ordered softmax aggregation (Dji = sigmoid(δji·d(i,j)/σ), silhouette AO = 1 − Π(1−Dji); L321-334, L459-469) replaces last-writer-wins with per-triangle contributions; Modular Primitives' own critique is damning: "Soft Rasterizer... tests each triangle for every pixel, and consequently loses to our method by several orders of magnitude" (L1250-1253), and the blur "makes opaque surfaces become transparent around edges, leading to an incorrect image. Optimization thus requires tuning these parameters" (L259-263) — a fundamental rework of the fill semantics, fallback-only. (4) edge-sampling / boundary integral (PSDR family) — in the PBR context needs Monte-Carlo boundary sampling with runtime silhouette detection that "does not scale well to complex geometry" (zhangPathspaceDifferentiableRendering2020.txt L632-637); the rasterization-adjacent form is Modular Primitives' analytic AA (the documented fallback), and the R2-4 FD-twin gate decides whether it is needed at all. (5) SDF reparameterization (Bangaru 2022 / Wang 2024) — requires an SDF representation + sphere tracing/ray marching + warp construction, all absent from the codebase; for a fixed STL this is pure overhead (the strategy exists for shape-DEFORMATION and neural-SDF reconstruction, not rigid pose). Topological derivatives (Mehta 2023) — level-set evolution with hole/phase nucleation for topology-changing reconstruction; a rigid 6-DoF pose has no topology changes, N/A, with one theory note worth keeping: "visibility terms in SDs are evaluated only on the apparent contours of the visible shape" (abstract/intro) — the theory-level confirmation that contour-only gradients are the norm for visibility, matching the MVP's EDGE-set-only gradient. [Sources: corpus — l/liuSoftRasterizerDifferentiable2019.txt, l/laineModularPrimitivesHighPerformance2020.txt, z/zhangPathspaceDifferentiableRendering2020.txt, b/bangaruDifferentiableRenderingNeural2022.txt, w/wangSimpleApproachDifferentiable2024.txt, m/mehtaTheoryTopologicalDerivatives2023.txt]
- A 2003 in-corpus clinical precedent for the edge-pixel gradient strategy: Livyatan et al., "Gradient-Based 2-D/3-D Rigid Registration of Fluoroscopic X-Ray to CT" (TMI 22(11), livyatanGradientbased2D3D2003.txt) — a three-stage "funnelling" pipeline (initial pose → coarse contour-based → fine "gradient projection registration (GPR) on edge pixels"), the fine stage explicitly "has a narrow convergence range" (L273-274, L302), with mean TRE 0.5–1.7 mm (L22-23). A DIRECT-like coarse stage + edge-pixel-gradient fine stage is exactly the polish's architecture, field-validated in 2D/3D fluoroscopy registration for two decades. [Source: corpus — l/livyatanGradientbased2D3D2003.txt]
- Confidence: high (all primary texts read directly this round; the ranking is an implementation-cost judgment grounded in the round-1/2 kernel facts).
- Relevance to this project: answers dispatch item (1) — the MVP's analytic design is the cheapest gradient strategy in the set; nothing in the corpus upgrades SoftRas/SDF/PSDR from fallback/N-A status; two round-1/2 "could not be verified" items are closed, including the z/w policy that anchored the depth-channel NO-GO.

#### R3-2 — The DiffDRR family does NOT change the 'no torch in the cost path' boundary — it confirms it, and supplies two measured facts for the polish
- DiffDRR (gopalakrishnanFastAutoDifferentiableDigitally2022.txt, in-corpus) exists because "most DRR generators do not offer a straightforward way to obtain gradients" (L22-23); its solution is to reformulate Siddon's method as vectorized tensor ops in PyTorch and lean on autodiff. The polish's analytic 2×6 projection Jacobian is the low-level answer to the same problem with no autodiff anywhere — the family's existence is evidence FOR the boundary, not against it: JTML already has, in closed form, what DiffDRR had to build torch to get. [Source: corpus — g/gopalakrishnanFastAutoDifferentiableDigitally2022.txt L22-28]
- LEAP (kimDifferentiableForwardProjector2023.txt, in-corpus) is the alternative engineering pattern: "core C++/CUDA module, Python binding and PyTorch interfaces" (L183-185, L236-241) — hand-written CUDA behind a thin torch.nn.Module binding, in XCT (voxel line integrals), NOT silhouette registration. The matched-projector doctrine is verbatim: "one should employ methods for backprojection that are the exact transpose of the forward projection, referred to as matched projectors... stable after over a thousand or more iterations, we chose to implement methods where the exact transpose is used" (L210-221) — the R2-4 gradient-twin gate is the rasterization-side implementation of this doctrine (the analytic gradient must equal the FD twin of the same forward). [Source: corpus — k/kimDifferentiableForwardProjector2023.txt L210-221]
- Two measured facts inside DiffDRR that harden the polish's premise: (a) the community baseline before differentiable DRRs was Nelder-Mead — "many applications use iterative gradient-free methods, such as the Nelder-Mead method [11], to optimize an image similarity metric" (L64-66) — primary-text support for arm D (R3-3); (b) "the loss landscapes for slice-to-volume registration in particular is convex in a large region around the optimum, making this problem better suited for gradient-based optimization methods" (L67-68), measured for negative ZNCC over ±30 mm / ±90° (L360-370) — the field's measured evidence that image-similarity landscapes are locally convex in the basin, the premise the surrogate-gradient relies on. Their 6-DoF gradient descent used per-axis update rates "because they have different units (βθϕγ = 5.3×10⁻² and βxyz = 7.5×10¹), and momentum λ = 0.9" (L628-630) — primary-text confirmation of the per-axis-scaling necessity behind the h·sign(g) / ADAM-lite design (R2-2/R2-6), and of Nicolet et al.'s "fewer and larger steps" preconditioning argument (nicoletLargeStepsInverse2021.txt L62-65; the (I+λL)^-p sparse-system machinery itself is mesh-space-specific and does NOT transfer to a 6-DoF pose — the transferable part is the per-axis preconditioning, which ADAM-lite already is). [Sources: corpus — g/gopalakrishnanFastAutoDifferentiableDigitally2022.txt; n/nicoletLargeStepsInverse2021.txt]
- Boundary verdict: unchanged. The convention governs the PRODUCTION cost path (DIRECT_DILATION and its metrics stay torch-free); the DRR/z-line-integral channel is the ML pathway, where the DiffDRR/LEAP pattern (hand-written CUDA core; torch only as an optional binding) is the documented reference if that pathway is ever built — same conclusion as round 1, now with two primary texts. [Source: angle 06 Round 1 "feasibility verdicts" (torch bridge NO-GO); corpus — g/gopalakrishnanFastAutoDifferentiableDigitally2022.txt, k/kimDifferentiableForwardProjector2023.txt]
- Confidence: high.
- Relevance: answers the second half of dispatch item (1) — the boundary holds; the family adds two measured facts (locally-convex basin; NM as the field baseline) that harden the polish's premise and its ablation design.

#### R3-3 — The simplex precedent: Mahfouz's optimizer IS a 7-point Nelder-Mead simplex with SA temperature; the ablation gains arm D (plain NM polish), and C-vs-D isolates the gradient's marginal value
- Primary text (mahfouzRobustMethodRegistration2003.txt, in-corpus): "Our SA algorithm is a modified version of the Nelder–Mead [30] (downhill simplex) optimization method. A simplex is a set of seven points where each point represents a possible pose, along with the value of the function space at that point. The algorithm iteratively perturbs the worst (highest) point of the simplex, in the direction of a lower score" (L451-454, L473-474); SA = "adds or subtracts a positive, logarithmically distributed random variable, proportional to the temperature, to the function values in the simplex", temperature "decreased every 40 iterations by multiplying the current temperature by 0.99", periodic simplex expansion (L479-488); termination "when the difference between the best and worst points in the simplex is less than a small threshold" (L490-491); ~0.2 s/iteration on a 1998 SGI Octane (L489). [Source: corpus — m/mahfouzRobustMethodRegistration2003.txt L451-491]
- The repo already dropped the SA ("Not Using Simulated Annealing Obviously..." — src/compute/implant_mahfouz_metric.cu:249-251); the polish should keep it dropped, and Mahfouz's own T=0 control is the primary-text justification: "with temperature equal to zero, the algorithm becomes a simple gradient descent algorithm that just traverses downhill to the nearest local minimum. We found, as expected, that the algorithm quickly fell into a local minimum near its starting point" (L597-602). That is the CORRECT behavior for a polish (the DIRECT trunk already did the basin selection; the polish must not escape the basin it was handed — SA's escape machinery is the global-search feature the polish deliberately does not want). Plain NM is the Mahfouz-validated local search at zero gradient cost. [Source: corpus — m/mahfouzRobustMethodRegistration2003.txt L597-602; repo — src/compute/implant_mahfouz_metric.cu:249-251]
- Design change (concrete): the R2-5 three-arm study becomes FOUR arms — D: DIRECT@34k + simplex-polish@B_p = 1000, where the polish is a 7-point Nelder-Mead on the chamfer surrogate: the shared ~35-line ChamferSurrogate wrapper from R2-2, standard reflection/expansion/contraction per nelderSIMPLEXMETHODFUNCTION1965.txt (P* = (1+α)P − αPh; expansion γ > 1; contraction 0 < β < 1; failed-contraction shrink toward the lowest point, L40-70), the initial simplex built from the leaf-box ranges scaled by the R2-2 h defaults, termination = simplex spread < threshold (Mahfouz's criterion) or B_p exhausted, every surrogate AND trial-verification eval incrementing cost_function_calls_ exactly as in arms B/C. Implementation: ~150-200 host lines, ZERO new kernels, no h-calibration, no barycentric staging — the cheapest polish of the four by construction. ### Summary

This round moved the polish MVP's evidence base onto the in-library primary texts and changed two design decisions. (1) The corpus survey ranks the five dispatch-named gradient strategies against JTML's hand-written CUDA rasterizer: the analytic edge-pixel gradient (the R2-4 design) is confirmed the cheapest — Modular Primitives (now in-corpus) is literally a rasterizer + pixel-dense scatter-add backward, of which the MVP is the rigid-body reduction — while SoftRas coverage, SDF reparameterization, path-space edge sampling, and topological derivatives are more expensive or N/A for a fixed-STL 6-DoF pose; the DiffDRR family does NOT change the 'no torch in the cost path' boundary (DiffDRR exists precisely because low-level CUDA generators lack gradients — the analytic Jacobian is the low-level answer; LEAP documents the CUDA-core-plus-thin-binding pattern JTML already matches). ### Key Findings

#### R3-1 — The corpus survey: the analytic edge-pixel gradient is the cheapest strategy; the reference implementation is in-library and two round-1/2 open items are resolved
- The R2-3/R2-4 design verified against the primary text (laineModularPrimitivesHighPerformance2020.txt): the rasterizer forward outputs "a 2D sample grid, with each position storing a tuple (ID, u, v, zc/wc)" (L549-552) plus "a buffer with the 2×2 Jacobian of the barycentrics w.r.t. the screen coordinates Juv = ∂{u,v}/∂{x,y}" (L561-562); the backward is "a dense operation over output pixels, using a scatter-add operation to accumulate the gradients from the pixels to the correct vertices based on the triangle IDs" (L589-594); analytic AA is a SEPARATE post-shading stage — "point-sampled visibility causes aliasing at visibility discontinuities, and more crucially, cannot produce visibility-related gradients for vertex positions. Antialiasing converts the discontinuities to smooth changes, from which the gradients can be computed" (L751-762) — exactly the R2-4 structure (pixel-grid kernel + ordered reduction + the AA fallback if the FD-twin gate says the boundary term matters). [Source: corpus — l/laineModularPrimitivesHighPerformance2020.txt]

[Source: corpus — l/laineModularPrimitivesHighPerformance2020.txt L903-904, L920-924]

[Source: corpus — k/kimDifferentiableForwardProjector2023.txt L210-221]
- Two measured facts inside DiffDRR that harden the polish's premise: (a) the community baseline before differentiable DRRs was Nelder-Mead — "many applications use iterative gradient-free methods, such as the Nelder-Mead method [11], to optimize an image similarity metric" (L64-66) — primary-text support for arm D (R3-3); (b) "the loss landscapes for slice-to-volume registration in particular is convex in a large region around the optimum, making this problem better suited for gradient-based optimization methods" (L67-68), measured for negative ZNCC over ±30 mm / ±90° (L360-370) — the field's measured evidence that image-similarity landscapes are locally convex in the basin, the premise the surrogate-gradient relies on. Their 6-DoF gradient descent used per-axis update rates "because they have different units (βθϕγ = 5.3×10⁻² and βxyz = 7.5×10¹), and momentum λ = 0.9" (L628-630) — primary-text confirmation of the per-axis-scaling necessity behind the h·sign(g) / ADAM-lite design (R2-2/R2-6), and of Nicolet et al.'s "fewer and larger steps" preconditioning argument (nicoletLargeStepsInverse2021.txt L62-65; the (I+λL)^-p sparse-system machinery itself is mesh-space-specific and does NOT transfer to a 6-DoF pose — the transferable part is the per-axis preconditioning, which ADAM-lite already is). [Sources: corpus — g/gopalakrishnanFastAutoDifferentiableDigitally2022.txt; n/nicoletLargeStepsInverse2021.txt]
- Boundary verdict: unchanged. The convention governs the PRODUCTION cost path (DIRECT_DILATION and its metrics stay torch-free); the DRR/z-line-integral channel is the ML pathway, where the DiffDRR/LEAP pattern (hand-written CUDA core; torch only as an optional binding) is the documented reference if that pathway is ever built — same conclusion as round 1, now with two primary texts. [Source: angle 06 Round 1 "feasibility verdicts" (torch bridge NO-GO); corpus — g/gopalakrishnanFastAutoDifferentiableDigitally2022.txt, k/kimDifferentiableForwardProjector2023.txt]
- Confidence: high.
- Relevance: answers the second half of dispatch item (1) — the boundary holds; the family adds two measured facts (locally-convex basin; NM as the field baseline) that harden the polish's premise and its ablation design.

#### R3-3 — The simplex precedent: Mahfouz's optimizer IS a 7-point Nelder-Mead simplex with SA temperature; the ablation gains arm D (plain NM polish), and C-vs-D isolates the gradient's marginal value
- Primary text (mahfouzRobustMethodRegistration2003.txt, in-corpus): "Our SA algorithm is a modified version of the Nelder–Mead [30] (downhill simplex) optimization method. A simplex is a set of seven points where each point represents a possible pose, along with the value of the function space at that point. The algorithm iteratively perturbs the worst (highest) point of the simplex, in the direction of a lower score" (L451-454, L473-474); SA = "adds or subtracts a positive, logarithmically distributed random variable, proportional to the temperature, to the function values in the simplex", temperature "decreased every 40 iterations by multiplying the current temperature by 0.99", periodic simplex expansion (L479-488); termination "when the difference between the best and worst points in the simplex is less than a small threshold" (L490-491); ~0.2 s/iteration on a 1998 SGI Octane (L489). [Source: corpus — m/mahfouzRobustMethodRegistration2003.txt L451-491]
- The repo already dropped the SA ("Not Using Simulated Annealing Obviously..." — src/compute/implant_mahfouz_metric.cu:249-251); the polish should keep it dropped, and Mahfouz's own T=0 control is the primary-text justification: "with temperature equal to zero, the algorithm becomes a simple gradient descent algorithm that just traverses downhill to the nearest local minimum. We found, as expected, that the algorithm quickly fell into a local minimum near its starting point" (L597-602). That is the CORRECT behavior for a polish (the DIRECT trunk already did the basin selection; the polish must not escape the basin it was handed — SA's escape machinery is the global-search feature the polish deliberately does not want). Plain NM is the Mahfouz-validated local search at zero gradient cost. [Source: corpus — m/mahfouzRobustMethodRegistration2003.txt L597-602; repo — src/compute/implant_mahfouz_metric.cu:249-251]
- Design change (concrete): the R2-5 three-arm study becomes FOUR arms — D: DIRECT@34k + simplex-polish@B_p = 1000, where the polish is a 7-point Nelder-Mead on the chamfer surrogate: the shared ~35-line ChamferSurrogate wrapper from R2-2, standard reflection/expansion/contraction per nelderSIMPLEXMETHODFUNCTION1965.txt (P* = (1+α)P − αPh; expansion γ > 1; contraction 0 < β < 1; failed-contraction shrink toward the lowest point, L40-70), the initial simplex built from the leaf-box ranges scaled by the R2-2 h defaults, termination = simplex spread < threshold (Mahfouz's criterion) or B_p exhausted, every surrogate AND trial-verification eval incrementing cost_function_calls_ exactly as in arms B/C. Implementation: ~150-200 host lines, ZERO new kernels, no h-calibration, no barycentric staging — the cheapest polish of the four by construction. Determinism: plain NM is RNG-free (unlike Mahfouz's SA version), and the surrogate value path is the same int-atomic-deterministic one, so rerun_identical is preserved. [Sources: corpus — n/nelderSIMPLEXMETHODFUNCTION1965.txt L40-70, m/mahfouzRobustMethodRegistration2003.txt L451-491; angle 06 R2-2/R2-5]
- Why arm D is included UNCONDITIONALLY (the dispatch's "if the surrogate valley is shallow" folds into the INTERPRETATION, not the inclusion): D costs one run column (~15 min/unit on the R2-5 matrix) and reuses only the shared wrapper; excluding the cheap control on a predicted gate would leave it unmeasured. Pre-registered interpretation: (i) C-vs-D at equal polish budget is the cleanest isolate of the gradient's marginal value — if the surrogate valley is deep (G1–G4 pass), the expectation is C ≥ D (the gradient uses ∇D information NM lacks); if the valley is shallow (G1 fails — the Yamazaki jagged-z-curve prior, R3-4), the expectation flips: D ≥ C on z and possibly on total cost, because NM's size-adapting reflection/contraction keeps making progress where a sign-step gradient stalls at the quantization floor; (ii) D-vs-B is the "local search is worth B_p evals at all" test independent of the gradient mechanism; (iii) if D ≈ C ≈ B, the polish hypothesis is dead at this budget — an honest null the three-arm design could not fully distinguish (C > B could have meant "local search in general helps", not "the gradient helps"). [Source: angle 06 R2-5; corpus — m/mahfouzRobustMethodRegistration2003.txt L597-602]
- Lineage note: NM-on-the-chamfer-surrogate is the closest faithful remnant of the DIRECT_MAHFOUZ lineage's optimizer (the metric's own 2003 paper used exactly a 7-point NM); the repo's divergence is about the annealing, not the simplex — arm D completes the lineage comparison angle 02 R3-1 opened. [Sources: repo — src/compute/implant_mahfouz_metric.cu:249-251; corpus — m/mahfouzRobustMethodRegistration2003.txt]
- Confidence: high on the mechanics (primary text + shared wrapper; NM is textbook host code); medium on the direction of the C-vs-D comparison (that is what the arm measures).
- Relevance: answers dispatch item (2) — the simplex-polish alternative is cheaper to implement than the gradient arms (no new kernels at all), has direct lineage, and its inclusion as arm D makes the ablation's polish conclusion unambiguous about WHERE the win (if any) comes from.

#### R3-4 — Yamazaki 2004: the dedicated depth-position paper uses a geometry/curve-fit remedy, not a gradient-type one — confirming the z-depth-channel NO-GO and upgrading the polish's z-arm to a decoupled fit
- The remedy, from the primary text (yamazakiImprovementDepthPosition2004.txt): after initial 6-DoF registration (Levenberg–Marquardt — a gradient-type method for the joint problem), depth position is optimized INDEPENDENTLY: the model is "moved along a straight line... joining the X-ray focus F... and the gravity center of the model G" (L265-269), depth sampled at "ten different points... over mm steps" (L370-371), RMSD computed at each, "the set of points... fitted to the polynomial" (L285-286), the extremum of the fitted polynomial taken as the depth optimum (L295-298), then "conventional 2-D/3-D registration was carried out a second time using the corrected depth position" (L300-302). Order selection measured: "for fourth- and higher-order polynomials, the extremum error is almost saturated (about 0.5 mm)" → order 4 (L380-383). Results: depth RMSE 2.6→0.9 mm (sim) / 3.2→1.4 mm (in vitro) (L28-29); residual ~0.5 mm bias "thought to be caused by slight errors in translation parallel to fluoroscopic images" (L629-631). NO depth channel, NO DRR, NO gradient of a z-term anywhere — the z signal is purely 2-D silhouette change: "a change in the depth position causes only small changes in the 2-D silhouette" (L14-15); "the accuracy of depth position is less than that for the other 5 DOF because the distance between the X-ray focus and the object is large, and as a result, the amount of information for changes in the projected 2-D silhouette is smaller than that for depth changes" (L104-107). [Source: corpus — y/yamazakiImprovementDepthPosition2004.txt]
- Interaction with the round-1 z-depth-channel NO-GO: CONFIRMS it from inside the field's own dedicated-depth paper. Yamazaki improves z by extracting MORE from the existing single-plane silhouettes (a 10-point curve fit), not by adding depth sensing — a front-surface z/w buffer would give the polish nothing to compare against, exactly as round 1 argued (no target depth in single-plane fluoro; z is magnification). The mechanism quote is the 2004 version of the round-1 observability argument: z accuracy is limited by the 2-D silhouette information, not by the optimizer. [Source: corpus — y/yamazakiImprovementDepthPosition2004.txt L104-107; angle 06 Round 1 "depth channel" finding]
- Three spec changes the primary text forces: (a) the polish's z-arm should be the DECOUPLED Yamazaki-style fit, not the gradient's z-component — "the evaluation curve for depth position was more jagged, and the curve peak less pointy" (L20-21, L620-621) and "the gradient of the curve changed markedly with distance between X-ray focus and the model" (L621-623) → "it is difficult to find an appropriate scale for depth position" (L626); Yamazaki's fit "does not require adjustment of the weight value" (L353-355). This is the primary-text version of the R2-1 G2 concern AND of the SAME_Z fixed-weight problem (a fixed z-weight fights a distance-dependent z-gradient scale). Concretely: the polish runs the gradient/simplex on the 5 in-plane DOFs with z handled either jointly (SAME_Z-weighted arm) or by the probe's yamazaki-polynomial mode (order-4 fit on the SAME 31-render sweep, angle 03 R3-2) as the terminal z stage — the ablation compares SAME_Z-weighted vs decoupled (already angle 03 R3-2's axis; the primary text now supplies the mechanism). (b) The sweep/perturbation direction should be the focus→COG ray, not the camera-z axis: for a centered implant these coincide; for an off-center implant the leaf z-axis differs by the off-axis angle — the R2-2 h_z = 8 mm default and the probe's ±15 mm sweep both assume camera-z; record the off-axis angle (and, cheaply, perturb along the ray). (c) The "jagged" z-curve prior feeds the precondition gate: G1's 0.10 valley-depth threshold is the right weak bar (a jagged-but-V-shaped curve still passes), and G2 (chamfer vs dilated) remains the discriminating gate — the R2-1 design, now with a primary-text prior that the z curve is the jagged one in THIS anatomy class. [Sources: corpus — y/yamazakiImprovementDepthPosition2004.txt L20-21, L352-355, L620-626; angle 03 R3-2; angle 06 R2-1/R2-2]
- Independent 2003 corroboration from the DIRECT_MAHFOUZ lineage: "the registration method is much less sensitive to displacements in that direction. Any single-plane registration method will be less accurate along the line of sight direction" (L646-648, L972-973); under occlusion "the registration method consistently estimated the position of the implant as being too far away... the position is primarily determined by the apparent size of the silhouette in the image" (L707-712) — the 2003 primary-text versions of the run's z-weak-axis and z-observable-only-via-scale findings (the round-1 "no gradient changes what is observable" claim now appears twice independently in the corpus, 2003 and 2004). [Source: corpus — m/mahfouzRobustMethodRegistration2003.txt L644-648, L707-712, L972-973]
- Confidence: high on the primary-text facts; medium on transferring Yamazaki's exact numbers to JTML (different implant/model/calibration — that is what the harness measures).
- Relevance: answers dispatch item (3) — the remedy is geometry/curve-fit, not gradient-type; the z-depth-channel NO-GO stands, and the polish's z-arm is upgraded to the field-validated decoupled fit.
